description: Ārambha: the knot of Brahmā pierced, bliss from the void, tinkling and the unstruck sound heard in the body; the body divine, radiant and fragrant, the heart full (as the text says).
Ghaṭa: the breath goes in the middle, the posture is firm, the knot of Viṣṇu is pierced and a kettledrum sound arises in the great void (as the text says).
Paricaya: the mardala sound in the sky, the great void, then the bliss of the natural state (sahajānanda); the text says the yogin is free of fault, sorrow, old age, disease, hunger and sleep.
Niṣpatti: the knot of Rudra pierced, flute and vīṇā sounds; the mind becomes one, which the text calls rājayoga.

The sounds heard: at first like ocean, thunder-cloud, kettledrum and jharjhara; in the middle mardala, conch, bell and kāhala; at the end tiny bells, flute, vīṇā and bee; they become subtler as practice grows (4.84).

The yogin joined in samādhi, as the text describes him: body like wood, as if dead, no perception of smell, taste, form, touch or sound, mind neither asleep nor awake, no sense of heat or cold, pain or pleasure, honour or dishonour, as if asleep though awake, not seized by weapons or mantras.

The text says that when mind and breath dissolve a bliss arises (4.30), that in laya breath and out-breath have ceased and objects are not grasped (4.31), and that it is known to oneself and beyond speech (4.32).
The text lists as marks of success in haṭha: a lean body, a serene face, a distinct inner sound, very clear eyes, freedom from disease, mastery of bindu, kindled digestive fire and purified channels.
notes: The marks are the text's list, not offered as observed effects.

description: The text names outward signs when the channels are purified, such as leanness of the body and brightness.
notes: The text says the verse; the rest of the list in the skeleton entry is not in this segment.

description: The text names three grades of breath-practice marked by sweat, trembling and attaining a place. Restricted practice; summary only.
